Now it only does so for Class. The symbol action only fires for types declared in the compilation, so this change does nothing for referenced-assembly types (the reported scenario). Its only effect is that every [MessagePackObject] struct declared in the user's own project stops being analyzed. Those structs will no longer get MsgPack004 (missing Key), MsgPack005 (duplicate or mixed keys), MsgPack007, MsgPack011, MsgPack015 or MsgPack017. Invalid structs then compile without errors and fail or misbehave only at generation or run time. CheckValidMessagePackFormatterAttribute can also produce a null location. Before the change these problems were reported (or crashed). Now they vanish with no diagnostic, so an invalid type in the user's own project builds cleanly. This goes against N1 (failures must not pass silently) and N2.
